sections.h2: Who records a deed in Belmont County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages and related papers in Belmont County are filed with the recorder, whose office is in the St. Clairsville courthouse, 101 West Main Street. The recorder describes the job as keeping the county's land records accurate, indexed and open to the public, with more than 220 years of them on hand. Staff can explain how the records are arranged, but a title search is something you arrange separately.

Indexing is the part sellers rarely notice. Each document is indexed so that a searcher can build a chain of title, which shows every owner and every debt attached to the land. Accurate indexing is what lets a title searcher find a deed, a lien or a release later.

Belmont County was organized in November 1801 and named St. Clairsville its seat in 1803, so the books reach back more than two centuries. Wikipedia places the county along the Ohio River, and the recorder's own description of the work includes farm deeds, home mortgages, oil and gas leases and military discharge papers.

sections.h2: What does Belmont County charge to put a document on record?
sections.html:
The recorder's online calculator states a simple structure that follows Ohio Revised Code 317.32. Belmont County does not add the optional $5 document preservation fee, which the statute lets a county charge.

Belmont County Recorder fee structure
ServiceFee
First two pages of a document$34
Each additional page$8
Each indexed marginal notation (reference)$4
Document that misses the layout standard$20 extra

Source: Belmont County Recorder fee calculator.

In the statute, the first two pages carry a $17 base fee and a second $17 for the housing trust fund. Each added page carries a $4 base and a $4 trust fund share. The statute sends any preservation surcharge to the county general fund, and the trust fund share is collected under section 317.36. Other services carry their own statutory rates:

  • Certified copy: a $1 base fee and a $1 trust fund fee per page, plus 50 cents and 50 cents when the recorder's seal is needed.
  • Photocopy at the counter: $1 and $1 per page.
  • Each marginal reference: $2 and $2, which matches the $4 in the table.
  • Living will or health care power of attorney: a base fee of $17 to $20 plus a matching trust fund fee.

Payment is due when the paper is handed in, except that electronic filers may settle by funds transfer or ACH afterward. The calculator is the quickest way to price a deed with several pages of legal description.

sections.h2: What layout rules apply to a deed recorded in Belmont County?
sections.html:
Documents must meet the standards in section 317.114, which the recorder summarizes on its document standards page. A document that falls short is still recorded, with a $20 surcharge.

  • Text set in at least 10-point type.
  • Sheets between letter size (8 1/2 by 11) and legal size (8 1/2 by 14).
  • Ink in black or blue, with highlighter left off the page.
  • Three inches of blank space above the text on page one, then an inch and a half on each page after.
  • One inch free along both sides and the bottom edge.

The rules do not apply to papers from a court or taxing authority, plats, exhibits, DD-214 discharge papers, state or federal documents, or any document signed before the law took effect in July 2009.

sections.h2: What documents does a Belmont County recorder have to file?
sections.html:
Section 317.08 lists what goes into the official records, and the list explains why more than deeds pass through the counter. Items most relevant to a house sale include:

  • Deeds and other instruments that convey land outright.
  • Mortgages, with their amendments, modifications and extensions.
  • Executory installment contracts for land that run more than a year.
  • Options to purchase, which must state a specific day and year of expiration.
  • Powers of attorney and memoranda of trust.
  • Declarations and bylaws for condominiums under Chapter 5311.
  • Easements, environmental covenants and conservation easements under the listed statutes.

For a seller the important point is that a recorded mortgage, option or contract stays in the public record until a release or other instrument is recorded against it. Ask a title company to check the county's records for a paid-off mortgage whose release was never recorded.

sections.h2: What happens before the recorder sees a Belmont County deed?
sections.html:
The auditor's office sits in the same courthouse and acts on the deed. Under section 319.202, the auditor does not endorse a deed until the grantee or a representative submits a statement declaring the value of the property, or a statement of the reason for exemption. The deed transfer desk takes calls at 740-699-2136, and the real estate desk at 740-699-2132.

A common order in Ohio counties, which Belmont County's offices can confirm, runs like this:

  • Draft the deed with the legal description and parcel number.
  • Take the deed and value statement to the auditor, pay the conveyance fee and get the endorsement.
  • Present the endorsed deed to the recorder with the fee.
  • Receive the recorded original or a return by mail.

Ask the auditor's deed transfer desk for the current conveyance rate, since counties set their own transfer tax within the limit in the statute. Ask the recorder's staff whether the recorded deed can be returned by mail.

sections.h2: What does the local market mean for a Belmont County seller?
sections.html:
In the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures, the typical owned home is valued at $154,900, and 73.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Nearly 91 percent of residents (90.9 percent) were in the same house a year earlier, so title often sits unchanged for years and older deeds are common. The 2020 census counted 31,618 housing units, and 13.6 percent of them stood vacant. Owners spend a median $1,215 a month with a mortgage and $489 without one. People 65 and older make up 24.9 percent of the population.

Estimated population slipped 3.1 percent from the April 2020 base to July 2025. The county's protected areas include Barkcamp State Park, Dysart Woods and the Egypt Valley Wildlife Area, and its lakes include Piedmont Lake and Belmont Lake. A house near any of them is sold on the same recorded title as one in town.

If a deed has gaps, such as a missing heir or a lien never released, the recorder cannot fix it. Clear it up through a title company or attorney before a new deed goes on record.

faqs.q: What is the price of recording a deed in Belmont County?
faqs.a: Per the recorder's calculator, the first two pages run $34 and every page after costs $8. A $4 fee applies to each indexed reference, and a document that misses the layout standard costs $20 more. The county does not add the optional $5 preservation fee.

faqs.q: Where is the Belmont County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: Find it inside the St. Clairsville courthouse (101 West Main Street, Ohio 43950), under the same roof as the auditor and treasurer. Deed transfers start at the auditor's desk, which takes calls at 740-699-2136.

faqs.q: What paper size and ink does the recorder require?
faqs.a: Print on letter or legal paper in black or blue ink, at 10 point or larger, with no highlighter. Keep the top margin at 3 inches on page one and 1 1/2 inches after that, and leave 1 inch at the sides and bottom. A document that misses these standards costs $20 more to record.

faqs.q: Does the recorder search my title?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's staff will explain how the records are arranged but will not perform title searches. Hire a title company or attorney for that, and expect a lender or buyer to ask for the result before closing.

faqs.q: Do I need the auditor before I record a Belmont County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, start with the auditor. The auditor's endorsement under section 319.202 depends on a statement of value, or a statement giving the reason for an exemption. Ask the recorder's staff how an endorsed deed should be delivered.
